expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: there's a window where old instances — still selecting `legacy_email` — run against a schema where it no longer exists. That's `UndefinedColumn` errors

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: Today: deploy only the code... Next week: the `DROP`, as its own deploy, once the code has baked

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: `git revert` does not bring the data back; only a restore from backup does

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: point-in-time recovery of the whole database plus re-applying everything written since

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: Timing isn't superstition — it's staffing math

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: block any changed migration containing `DROP`/`TRUNCATE`/`ALTER … DROP` unless the PR carries an explicit approval label

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: ship half of it this afternoon, not the drop

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: The `DROP COLUMN` is. The code change isn't — that reverts in minutes
